description: Biodiversity, species diversity, conservation, and the sixth mass extinction

entries.definition: The variety of life on Earth at all its levels, from genes to ecosystems; encompasses the evolutionary, ecological, and cultural processes that sustain life

levels.genetic: Variation in genes within a species
levels.species: Variety of species in a region

scale_of_life.estimated_species: 8.7 million eukaryotic species estimated; only ~1.5 million formally described
scale_of_life.least_known: Deep sea, soil microbiomes, tropical forest canopy

biodiversity_hotspots.definition: Regions with exceptional concentrations of endemic species under exceptional threat
biodiversity_hotspots.criteria: Must have 1,500+ endemic plant species AND lost 70%+ of original vegetation
biodiversity_hotspots.total: 36 hotspots covering 2.4% of Earth's land but containing 77% of all biodiversity

examples.madagascar: 90%+ species found nowhere else; 95% of original forest lost
examples.coral_triangle: 6 million km²; 75% of coral species; SE Asia
examples.mediterranean_basin: Cradle of Western civilization; high plant endemism
examples.amazon: 10% of all species; under severe threat from deforestation

sixth_mass_extinction.context: Five previous mass extinctions in Earth's history; worst was Permian-Triassic (96% species lost)
sixth_mass_extinction.status: World Wildlife Fund: 69% decline in vertebrate populations since 1970

threatened_species.critically_endangered: Amur leopard, Javan rhinoceros, Sumatran orangutan, vaquita porpoise (<10 individuals)

causes.habitat_loss: Primary driver; 75% of land significantly altered
causes.climate_change: Increasingly important; shifts habitats, alters seasons

importance_of_biodiversity.food_security: 3 crops (wheat, rice, maize) provide 60% of human caloric intake; wild relatives crucial for breeding
importance_of_biodiversity.medicine: 50%+ of drugs derived from or inspired by natural products
importance_of_biodiversity.ecosystem_services: Biodiversity underpins pollination, pest control, water purification
importance_of_biodiversity.resilience: More diverse ecosystems more stable and resistant to change

conservation_approaches.protected_areas: 17% of land, 10% of ocean currently protected; 30x30 target by 2030
conservation_approaches.corridor_conservation: Connecting fragmented habitats for wildlife movement
conservation_approaches.community_conservation: Indigenous and local communities as stewards
conservation_approaches.rewilding: Restore large-scale natural processes; reintroduce keystone species

keystone_species.definition: Species whose impact on ecosystem is disproportionately large

examples.sea_otter: Eats sea urchins; prevents kelp forest destruction
examples.wolf: Yellowstone; controls elk; allows riverbank vegetation recovery
examples.elephant: African ecosystem engineer; creates water holes; disperses seeds
examples.fig_tree: Provides fruit year-round; keystone for hundreds of species
